quest.title: Aesthetic Critique: Practice of Aesthetics
quest.description: Depierris the artist seems to have another new idea...

dialogues.speaker: Depierris
dialogues.text: This is a good idea... but can it really be done this way...?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: How's the drawing going?

dialogues.speaker: Depierris
dialogues.text: Ah it's you! Thanks for your help previously with the photos! The sights they featured were truly inspiring.

dialogues.speaker: Depierris
dialogues.text: I already have an approximate idea, and I've drawn up some drafts, but... Well, they're not up to snuff.

dialogues.speaker: Depierris
dialogues.text: Don't misunderstand — this is not to say that I've painted some trash with no aesthetic value at all, but...

dialogues.speaker: Depierris
dialogues.text: I feel that they're missing something special, something that can help them transcend the ordinary.

dialogues.speaker: Depierris
dialogues.text: There's something too concrete about the things I have in mind... If I directly translated them into my painting, the beauty I wish to transmit will be damaged for sure.

dialogues.speaker: Depierris
dialogues.text: *sigh* I fear this is a problem that every artist must face...

choices.text: Perhaps you could try drawing something else?

response.speaker: Depierris
response.text: Thanks for the suggestion, but I fear that this problem will not be solved by a mere change of topics.

response.speaker: Depierris
response.text: Whether it be mountains and rivers, birds and beasts, or the world of humanity... None of them can escape this issue.

response.speaker: Depierris
response.text: It is precisely in their search for a solution that some of my colleagues have broken down and transmuted the sights they've seen using their inner feelings.

response.speaker: Depierris
response.text: Such art emphasizes one's inner emotions most of all, and the result on the canvas is... How can I explain it...

response.speaker: Depierris
response.text: Well, whether it be characters, scenery... Even light carries a sense of strangeness that no traditional sense of aesthetics can capture.

response.speaker: Depierris
response.text: A simplistic glance would lead most to believe these paintings to be the brainchildren of the illiterate in art, or the mad.

response.speaker: Depierris
response.text: But if you calm your spirit and get in tune with the artwork before you, you will hear it roar on the artist's behalf.

response.speaker: Depierris
response.text: That roar comes from the artist's heart and soul, speaking their feelings aloud... and those feelings are, more often than not, rather intense.

response.speaker: Depierris
response.text: Yet their voices cannot be perceived by the ear, but with the heart instead.

response.speaker: Depierris
response.text: As for me... I do not yet wish to give in on the concrete, and so I've come up with another way.

response.speaker: Depierris
response.text: I have decided to focus on color, and so I need to find stronger shades and simple yet powerful strokes.

response.speaker: Depierris
response.text: At the same time, I need to weaken the lighting and traditional scene compositions... These things will affect my expression, and so I must ask them to temporarily leave the scene...

response.speaker: Depierris
response.text: But the issue is that the strong, intense colors dictate the use of a lot of paint, and that I need to squeeze the paint directly onto the canvas to achieve the necessary effect.

response.speaker: Depierris
response.text: So, I've... uh, run out of paint. However, I cannot simply move my easel away at the moment. That would surely affect my creative work...

response.speaker: Depierris
response.text: Traveler, could I trouble you to visit Boucicaut? I've ordered a batch of good paints from him, and they should be ready at this point.

response.speaker: Depierris
response.text: Or perhaps... Could you help me get some Whopperflower Nectar? That way, I could make a batch of paints on my own.

choices.text: You can use nectar to make paint?

response.speaker: Depierris
response.text: Hahaha, of course you can. Some of my fellow artists even use Bird Eggs for that task!

response.speaker: Depierris
response.text: I hear that paints of this kind have delicate colors but rich layers, perfect for use in depicting resplendent sceneries.

response.speaker: Depierris
response.text: You're a good soul, aren't you? Would you refuse an artist's plaintive plea?

response.speaker: Depierris
response.text: Alright, thank you so much! I'll wait here. Just bring them straight back to me once you get them.

choices.text: You're hopeless... Just leave it to me.

response.speaker: Depierris
response.text: Hahaha, of course! That's the first thing you should learn as a painter — that's how you retain control over the image you create.

choices.text: Why don't you try a different painting style?

response.speaker: Depierris
response.text: That's right. Some of my colleagues thought so too, and they are presently attempting to use some "figurative" methods of painting to produce something more abstract.

response.speaker: Depierris
response.text: The most radical amongst them even wish to give up on depicting concrete objects altogether and simply use splotches of paint to express themselves... They call themselves "Neodescriptionists."

response.speaker: Depierris
response.text: But I must say that even I cannot quite grasp their work. At most, I can only sense the rhythmic beauty contained within the colored splotches and line work...

response.speaker: Depierris
response.text: As for what any given painting really expresses... I can only ask that painter to explain it to me.

dialogues.speaker: Boucicaut
dialogues.text: Hello. What would you like to buy?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'm here for Depierris's paints...

dialogues.speaker: Boucicaut
dialogues.text: Oh, you're here to get paints for him? I've got them right here.

dialogues.speaker: Boucicaut
dialogues.text: He really does use them up very quickly. You'd think he pours them straight into the water after buying them!

dialogues.speaker: Boucicaut
dialogues.text: Well, regardless, here they are. Take them to him, would you?

dialogues.speaker: Depierris
dialogues.text: Traveler, have you gotten the things I need? Hehe. Now then, did you bring paints, or Whopperflower nectar?

dialogues.speaker: Depierris
dialogues.text: Thank you! These paints should last me for a while.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Don't spill them all into the water.

dialogues.speaker: Depierris
dialogues.text: Into the water? Hahaha. I suppose my painting technique is just as you describe.

dialogues.speaker: Depierris
dialogues.text: But only by squeezing the paint out and directly pouring it out onto the canvas before using a carving blade and palette knife will provide me with the touch necessary to make an impact on others.

dialogues.speaker: Depierris
dialogues.text: Thanks for your help. I should be able to continue with the aid of these paints. Come over and take a look when you have the time, alright?

dialogues.speaker: Depierris
dialogues.text: It is all thanks to your help that my work has started out on the right foot, after all.

dialogues.speaker: Depierris
dialogues.text: Once this painting is complete, I hope that you'll be the first to come appreciate it.

dialogues.speaker: Depierris
dialogues.text: This nectar is not bad! Very good — great paint shall surely come of this.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What sort of paints do you want to make?

dialogues.speaker: Depierris
dialogues.text: Hmm... I'd like to make ones that lean towards warm shades, but with a melancholy touch.

dialogues.speaker: Depierris
dialogues.text: They'll also need to be thick enough to allow me to work with compact brushstrokes.

dialogues.speaker: Depierris
dialogues.text: Thanks for your help. I should be able to continue with the aid of these paints. Come over and take a look when you have the time, alright?

dialogues.speaker: Depierris
dialogues.text: It is all thanks to your help that my work has started out on the right foot, after all.

dialogues.speaker: Depierris
dialogues.text: Once this painting is complete, I hope that you'll be the first to come appreciate it.

dialogues.speaker: Depierris
dialogues.text: We cannot be too restricted by concrete forms... We must draw the beauty out and use symbolic methods too...

dialogues.speaker: Depierris
dialogues.text: No, no... Still no. This composition is too deliberate...
